newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says Navy not involved in Filipino case.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says Navy not involved in Filipino case.

text.p: Malaysia's defence minister said on Monday a preliminary investigation showed that no Royal Malaysian Navy personnel were involved in the alleged detention of seven Filipinos in the southwestern Philippines.
Defence Minister Syed Hamid Albar said his ministry was conducting a complete probe into the incident, however, the official Bernama news agency reported.
On Sunday, Philippine President Fidel Ramos ordered an investigation into the alleged abduction by a group of Malaysians of seven Filipinos they suspected of stealing their boat engines.
A presidential palace statement, quoting police sources, said a vessel carrying several Malaysians docked at a village on Palawan island in the southwestern Philippines on April 14.

According to the statement, the Malaysians, whose vessel "...closely resembled (a) Malaysian naval patrol craft", loaded six fishermen and a 10-year-old boy into several motorboats and took them to Kudat, Malaysia, where they were being detained.

Syed Hamid, who spoke to reporters while at a function in northern Perak state, said: "My ministry will be communicating with the the military and police to obtain the actual information as both authorities conduct regular patrols in Malaysia's exclusive economic zone."
Piracy is rampant in the waters between Malaysia and the Philippines.
Syed Hamid said his Philippine counterpart had yet to contact him on the matter. But he said he would keep Manila informed of the investigations through Malaysia's foreign ministry.
Ramos had directed the minister of defence, foreign affairs and interior "to look into and take appropriate actions" on the matter, the presidential palace statement said.
